fieldNotes.facility: Positively identified as GM Arlington Assembly, the ~250-acre / 3.75M sq-ft full-size SUV plant (Tahoe, Suburban, Yukon, Escalade). Wikipedia infobox coords 32.7383,-97.0736 land directly on the main assembly building. Site is bounded by E Abram St on the south, TX-360 on the east, an active rail corridor on the north, and a wooded buffer behind a residential neighborhood on the west.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Entire property is fully fenced and access-controlled (masonry wall topped with steel fence visible along E Abram in Street View; perimeter fence/gates at all internal road tie-ins). Material-receiving and finished-vehicle traffic run through controlled GM gates (Waze tags a 'Gate 11' on Abram). Public Street View does not penetrate the gates, consistent with a guarded campus.
fieldNotes.guardShack: GM auto-assembly plants of this scale operate staffed security gatehouses at truck/material gates (same baseline confirmed at Ford Dearborn). Booth-scale structures sit beside the controlled internal-road entrances; high-confidence inference from fencing + GM standard practice.
fieldNotes.railServed: Multiple active rail spurs penetrate the north side of the property; long covered rail loading/auto-rack structures and strings of rail cars are clearly visible along the north/NE edge feeding the plant and the finished-vehicle marshalling area.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Vast finished-vehicle marshalling lots (thousands of stalls) along the east side fronting TX-360, plus trailer/auto-hauler staging near the north rail docks; trailer drop capacity is large (50+ band).
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated finished-vehicle and trailer staging lots separate from the active dock aprons, on the east and north of the building.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Inbound parts/material receiving concentrates on the west and north building faces near rail; finished-vehicle (shipping) marshalling is a physically separate cluster on the east toward TX-360.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide internal perimeter roads and large gate aprons give ample paved width to add express/bypass lanes.
fieldNotes.multiStep: Campus-scale security implies an outer perimeter gate then internal checkpoints before docks; not directly visible in Street View, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale positively identified in overhead imagery; left uncertain.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Estimate from overhead imagery; loading doors distributed across multiple building faces of a very large assembly building plus rail/parts receiving banks.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Inside the dense DFW metro fabric, immediately adjacent to the Arlington entertainment district (AT&T Stadium / Globe Life Field) and surrounded by residential and commercial development.
